source.title: Cessna Model 172N Pilot's Operating Handbook (1979 model)
source.copy_reviewed: Public scan cited in 04b_poh_reference/poh_1979_reference_data.json (teensinflight.org); the scan also contains an operator supplement for one UK-registered aircraft, which Phase 7 does not use.
source.method: Values below were read from the OCR text of that scan on 2026-11-06 and cross-checked against the page footer. Page numbers are POH page numbers (section-page).
source.second_copy: Entries marked "copy": "1978 handbook" were read on 2026-11-10 from the page images of a scan of the 1978 Model 172N handbook supplied by the author (no text layer: each value was read from the page itself). The two model years share these pages; where a later entry repeats an earlier one, the later one is the one that was read from the figure.

160 BHP at 2700 RPM
2280-2400 RPM (carb heat off, full rich)
min 25, green 60-90, max 100
6 (7 total with oil filter)
lower right side of the firewall
McCauley 1C160/DTM7557, fixed pitch, two blades, 75 in max / 74 in min
100LL (blue) or 100 (green)

27 gal each, 54 total, 50 usable
E red line; 1.5 gal unusable each standard tank (2.0 long range)
gravity feed; selector BOTH, RIGHT, LEFT, OFF; strainer; manual primer; carburetor
white 41-85, green 47-128, yellow 128-160, red line 160
engine-driven dual magneto, two plugs per cylinder
right magneto: lower right + upper left plugs; left magneto: lower left + upper right plugs
rotary OFF, R, L, BOTH, START (spring loaded back to BOTH)
at 1700 RPM; drop not more than 125 RPM on either magneto or 50 RPM differential
about 100-225 RPM with full heat at full throttle
up-draft, float type, fixed jet, accelerator pump, idle cut-off, manual mixture
lean until RPM peaks and drops 25-50 RPM; above 75% power do not lean beyond peak RPM
mixture RICH, carb heat COLD, master ON, prime 2-6 strokes (none if warm), throttle open 1/8 in, ignition START, oil pressure CHECK
mixture full lean, throttle full open, crank; repeat start without priming
28-volt DC, 60-amp alternator, 24-volt battery on left forward side of the firewall
split rocker: BAT (right half) all power, ALT (left half) alternator
shows battery charge or discharge rate
red LOW VOLTAGE light below ammeter; ACU removes alternator field on over-voltage; reset by recycling master; may illuminate at low RPM with load
avionics OFF, master OFF (both), master ON, light CHECK OFF, avionics ON; if again: alternator OFF, non-essential equipment OFF, terminate flight
airspeed 65 KIAS, carb heat ON, fuel selector BOTH, mixture RICH, ignition BOTH (or START if prop stopped), primer IN and LOCKED
alternate static source valve PULL ON; consult calibration tables in Section 5
flaps up, heater/vents and windows closed: 40->39, 50->51, ... 100->101, 140->141 KIAS
pitot tube on lower surface of left wing; static port lower left side of forward fuselage; optional heated pitot; optional alternate static valve below the throttle
gradual RPM loss; full throttle and full carb heat until smooth, then remove heat
engine-driven vacuum pump powers attitude and directional indicators; below 4.5 inHg indicators not reliable
span 36 ft, length 26 ft 11 in (envelope only)

wing span 36 ft (note 1: shown with strobe lights installed); length 26 ft 11 in; height 8 ft 9½ in maximum (note 2: nose gear depressed, all tires and nose strut properly inflated, flashing beacon installed); horizontal tail span 11 ft 4 in; main wheel track 8 ft 4½ in; propeller arc 6 ft 3 in maximum; note 3: wheel base 65 in; note 4: propeller ground clearance 11¾ in; note 5: wing area 174 sq ft; note 6: minimum turning radius, pivot point to outboard wing tip, 27 ft 5½ in

firewall station 0; rear doorpost bulkhead station 65.3 (65¼ in aft of the firewall); 48¾ in from the instrument panel to that bulkhead; 42¾ in further to the aft cabin wall (station 108); aft baggage area 34 in long, to station 142
41 ahead of the front seats, 48 at the front seats, 43 at the rear seat, 33 in the baggage area, 10¼ in the aft baggage area

at the lower window line / at the cabin floor: 39½ / 34 at the front seats; 37½ / 29½ between the rear door posts; 38½ / 36 behind them; 35 / 25 and 33½ / 28 in the baggage area; 21½ at the aft end of the aft baggage area
cabin door: 32 wide at the top, 37 at the bottom, 40 high in front, 41 high at the rear; baggage door: 15¼ wide at top and bottom, 22 high in front, 21 high at the rear

single-slot type; electrically driven; switch lever on the instrument panel in a slotted panel with mechanical stops at 10° and 20°; scale and pointer beside the lever show flap travel in degrees; 15-ampere FLAP circuit breaker

tricycle; steerable nose wheel, two main wheels, wheel fairings; tubular spring-steel main gear struts; air/oil nose gear shock strut; hydraulically actuated disc brake on the inboard side of each main wheel, with a fairing over each brake
two areas: from the back of the rear seats to the aft cabin bulkhead, and one aft of that bulkhead; lockable baggage door on the left side; baggage net with tie-down straps

occupant centre of gravity: pilot and front passenger station 37 with the seat set for an average occupant (34 to 46); rear passengers station 73; baggage area 1 station 82 to 108 (arm 95); baggage area 2 station 108 to 142 (arm 123); datum station 0 is the front face of the firewall

two separate adjustable front seats (four-way or six-way), a split-backed fixed rear seat, optional child's seat; four-way: tubular handle under the centre of the seat for fore and aft, lever under the right front corner for the seat back angle; rear seat backs adjusted with a lever under each corner of the seat bottom

seat belts at all seats, attached to fittings on the floorboard, buckle half inboard and link half outboard of each front seat; front shoulder harness attached to the rear doorpost above the window line and stowed behind a sheath above the cabin door; integrated harness with inertia reels optional

two entry doors with a recessed exterior handle, an interior handle (OPEN, CLOSE, LOCK), a key-operated lock on the left door only and a door stop mechanism; openable window in the left door (right optional), held closed by a detent equipped latch on the lower edge of the window frame, with a spring-loaded retaining arm; may be opened up to 160 knots
shaped steel rod with a red metal flag, through the hole in the top of the pilot's control wheel shaft and the hole in the shaft collar on the instrument panel; the flag covers the ignition switch
separate adjustable ventilators: one near each upper corner of the windshield, two available for the rear cabin area

audio control panel with transmitter selector switch, automatic audio selector switch and audio selector switches (speaker or phone); microphone-headset with a keying switch on the left side of the pilot's control wheel, jacks near the lower left corner of the instrument panel; static dischargers recommended for IFR

instrument panel figure names, among others: light rheostat control knobs, lighter, map compartment, microphone, auxiliary mike jack, phone jack, rear view mirror, omni course indicators, ADF bearing indicator

preflight inspection: control wheel lock REMOVE; rudder gust lock REMOVE; tail, wing and nose tie-downs DISCONNECT; pitot tube cover REMOVE; sampler cup at each fuel tank sump quick-drain valve; strainer drain knob pulled for about four seconds; oil not less than four quarts
the airplane is most easily moved by hand with a tow bar attached to the nose gear strut; towed by a vehicle, the nose wheel must never be turned more than 30 degrees either side of centre
